requirements.requirement: Provide the supplied project documents through a WebDAV workspace at /documents/ on node1 TCP port 8080.
requirements.summary: Apache is active and listening on port 8080. Authenticated PROPFIND and GET succeeded, listed both seeded documents, and returned content matching the originals; the same state was observed after restart.

requirements.requirement: Allow the editor account from access.txt to create, read, replace, and delete documents.
requirements.summary: Credentials were derived from access.txt, and a bounded test directly observed successful creation, reads with verified content, replacement, deletion, and a subsequent 404.

requirements.requirement: Honor exclusive document locks so an update without the lock token cannot overwrite a locked document.
requirements.summary: A lock token was acquired, a tokenless overwrite left the locked content unchanged, and an overwrite carrying the token changed the content as intended. Lock protection was exercised again after restart.

requirements.requirement: Prevent anonymous clients from accessing the workspace.
requirements.summary: Anonymous GET and PROPFIND returned 401 before restart, and anonymous GET again returned 401 after recovery.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the initial project documents in /srv/legacy2/webdav-document-locks.
requirements.summary: Final source hashes exactly match the preparation baseline for access.txt, brief.txt, and budget.csv. The source file inventory remained complete, and access.txt retained mode 600 with root ownership.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained CentOS Stream 10 on kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 before and after execution. Apache 2.4.63 was installed from the platform's configured AppStream repository.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied by direct behavioral and final-state evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for node1: it records a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot ID independently corroborated by lifecycle observations, and recovered service, data, authentication, firewall, and locking behavior.
limitations: Some HTTP lock-result values were redacted in captured stdout, so exact status codes such as 423 cannot be independently read. However, shell assertions directly establish that tokenless replacement did not alter content and token-bearing replacement did.

The lifecycle temporary-file inventory covers /tmp but not /var/tmp, so the apparent retention of the two restart-evidence files is inferred from their creation and the absence of a recorded cleanup rather than confirmed by a final directory inventory.
Requirement source-preservation cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: The implementation mutations were causally connected to installing, configuring, securing, testing, or restarting the WebDAV service. Test documents and /tmp request/response files were cleaned up, package health remained good, and no failed services appeared. Two small evidence artifacts were apparently retained: /var/tmp/webdav-pre-restart-boot-id created by cmd-583b1cb432d14b1a and /var/tmp/webdav-reboot.log created by cmd-daf6f63776fd4ebb; the trace shows no later removal. These are low-risk but unnecessary after verification. No other unnecessary mutations are evident.
